text:
Maya (oncall): Heads up — we're seeing a customer spike with repeated 503s, started ~2m ago. Multiple customers reporting timeouts and retries.
Jonah (infra): looking, seeing a flurry of upstream worker exits on pool-gpu-12. OOM-ish pattern in logs.
Maya (oncall): stack traces?
Jonah (infra): paste from node: 
```
[2026-03-18T15:12:02Z] infer-runner[pid=2345]: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f9e2a3b4f libnv*+0x5f0
[2026-03-18T15:12:02Z] OOM killer invoked: task infer-runner score 987
[2026-03-18T15:12:02Z] container restart by kubelet
```
Priya (cs): Customer-facing: Acme reported 110k failed requests in last 5m, attaching their request ids. They're on a Free tier but SLA-sensitive.
Maya (oncall): Impact map: hosted gateway is returning 503 for inference.v1.generate for ~15% of requests p95 latency doubled.
infra-bot: autoscaler scaled down pool-gpu-12 due to node churn, restarted 6 containers in 60s.
Jonah (infra): repro steps so far: heavy toolcall + long context (ctx ~120k tokens) triggers huge KV cache growth, then memory balloon on GPU -> driver pagefault -> segfault -> container exit.
Maya (oncall): can we confirm if this is quantized-runtime-specific?
Jonah (infra): initial repro used the quantized runtime (q8_0). I re-ran on non-quant (fp16) and it still OOMs but less consistently. Looks like the prefetch/kvcache and toolcall path are the common trigger.
Carl (support lead): Priya, please open CS thread, offer fallback to hosted-llm-small (CPU) while we mitigate. Note customer is asking about billing credits.
Priya (cs): on it. I've notified Acme and offered temporary route to cpu-small via feature-flag; they accepted.
Maya (oncall): mitigation ideas: 1) enable graceful backoff on kube restarts to avoid hot-restart storm; 2) temporary routing rule to divert requests with toolcall=true to a stable CPU pool; 3) patch runtime to limit KV prefetch memory per-request.
Jonah (infra): quick patch: add strict cgroup memlimit on runner pods in pool-gpu-12 and increase restart backoff to 60s. Deploying now.
infra-bot: deploy job started: infra/patches/9980012345-kv-prefetch-cgroup.yaml -> status: in_progress
Maya (oncall): after patch, monitoring... any change in 503 rate?
Jonah (infra): early signal: container restarts dropped from 12/min -> 1/min. 503 rate decreased to ~3%. Still seeing a few segfaults on very large contexts.
Priya (cs): Acme confirms reduced failures after switching flag. They asked for ETA on full fix.
Maya (oncall): action items: Jonah to capture full coredump and nvdriver logs for triage; Research to reproduce with a synthetic harness (large toolcall + kv prefetch). Priya to coordinate CS credits and update customer. Carl to prioritize rollback-safe patch to limit per-request kv prefetch bytes.
Jonah (infra): coredump saved to s3://redwood-debug/9980012345/coredump.tar.gz, nvlogs attached to ticket INF-4983. Repro harness link: https://ci.redwood/internal/repro/9980012345 (runs in approx 30m).
Maya (oncall): tagging as P1 until root cause patch is merged. Keep updates here every 15m.
Priya (cs): noted. I'll send an interim status to Acme with workaround details and expected timeline: 24-48h for a patch, ETA tighter if repro harness succeeds.
Jonah (infra): follow-up: found an allocator path that double-allocs when toolcall metadata contains large JSON tool args. Quick fix candidate in runtime-mem.c to cap tool-arg size to 64k. Will create a PR.
Maya (oncall): great. If PR looks safe, do canary rollout to pool-gpu-12 with circuit-breaker.
infra-bot: PR created: infra/runtime#2421 -> status: open -> reviewers: @Jonah, @Maya
Carl (support lead): CS note: log all customer impact numbers for billing review. Priya - keep me posted before offering credits.
Maya (oncall): next check in 15m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
